Investors chalk up some of the weakness to a lack of tax returns and concerns about a slowing labor market. The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts. That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. Spending at general merchandise stores fell 3% in March from the prior month and spending at gas stations declined 5.5% during the same period. In addition to water loss due to anintense multiyear drought, the US Geological Survey and the Bureau of Reclamationreport found, Lake Powell faced an average annual loss in storage capacity of about 33,270 acre-feet, or 11 billion gallons, per year between 1963 and 2018. That’s enough water to fill the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall about 1,600 times. The capacity of the reservoir is shrinking because of sediments flowing in from theColorado and San Juan rivers, according to the report. Those sediments settle at the bottom of the reservoir and decrease the total amount of water the reservoir can hold. As of Monday, Lake Powell was around 25% full, according to data from the Bureau of Reclamation. It’s bad news for a region already facing water shortages and extreme wildfires due to the drought. title: Drone hits US-owned gas storage vessel at Egypt's Damietta port as tensions escalate in West Asia
full_text: Drone hits US-owned gas storage vessel at Egypt's Damietta port as tensions escalate in West Asia Three trading sources familiar with the incident told Reuters the drone struck the floating storage tanker Energos Winter, causing a blaze that spread to Gaslog Salem. Two security sources said initial assessments indicated the explosion was likely caused by a drone strike A drone struck a US-owned floating gas storage tanker at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta on Wednesday, triggering a fire that spread to another vessel, British maritime security firm Ambrey said, in an incident that could signal a further widening of the conflict in West Asia. Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry confirmed a fire at the port but did not mention a drone attack or specify the cause of the incident. Port services firm Inchcape separately said two gas tankers caught fire at Damietta. Three trading sources familiar with the incident toldReutersthe drone struck the floating storage tanker Energos Winter, causing a blaze that spread to Gaslog Salem. Two security sources said initial assessments indicated the explosion was likely caused by a drone strike. British maritime risk management firm Vanguard said the Energos Winter was hit by an unidentified projectile on its starboard side, causing a fire that was later extinguished. It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the incident, which came shortly after Iran launched a missile attack on US forces in Jordan and the United States and Saudi Arabia carried out strikes on Iran-backed paramilitary groups in Iraq. The attack also followed US President Donald Trump’s threat to retaliate against Iran and the Houthis’ announcement of a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, marking a further escalation in the conflict since the United States and Israel began bombing Iran in February.
